verdict.rationale: Obsidian's own documentation says notes are plain-text files stored locally, and that Sync's default end-to-end encryption means no one, not even the Obsidian team, can access your notes. That structurally keeps vault content out of vendor hands, but the docs never mention AI training, a no-training policy, or an opt-out. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that user data is not used for AI model training, coverage of Publish-hosted content and plugin data flows, and independent corroboration of the policy.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models

citations.quote: Obsidian uses non-proprietary plain text Markdown files stored locally on your device. You have total control over your data
This guarantees that no one — not even the Obsidian team — can access your notes.
Obsidian Sync encrypts your remote vault and all communication with Obsidian's servers.
Notes are stored only on their machine and sync service
